text:
maya: Heads-up — I ran a couple of KV-cache quant experiments this morning combining INT8/FP8/4-bit for KV store and wanted to share profiling + a couple questions. Results look...interesting.

ryan: Nice. Short summary? p50/p99 numbers, mem, decode deltas?

maya: Quick TL;DR: INT8 KV gives ~18% GPU memory win vs FP16 baseline and ~12% token latency win in long-context decode on steady traffic. FP8 KV gives slightly more memory saving but decode quality drops rarely. 4-bit KV (w/ per-channel scale) hits the best memory numbers (~38% reduction) and latency (~25% lower) but we saw hallucination spikes on some prompts at long lengths.

olga: Can you paste the profiler traces and the command you used to generate them?

maya: Sure — I ran our standard decode-bench with batching set to 8 and sequence length 2048. Command:

```
./decode-bench --model=model-v2-13b --kv-quant={int8,fp8,int4} --batch=8 --seq=2048 --calib=online --kernels=auto --iters=300
```

Profiler snippet (timestamps stripped):

```
GPU usage peak: INT8-KV 12.1GB, FP8-KV 13.6GB, int4-KV 9.2GB
Avg token decode time (ms): FP16-KV: 9.8, INT8-KV: 8.6, FP8-KV: 8.4, INT4-KV: 7.3
Kernel split (INT4 run): GEMM 58%, KV-lookup 10%, Scale/unscale 12%, memcpy 15%, other 5%
```

maya: Important: the INT4 run spent more time in scale/unscale and had more frequent kernel-selection changes mid-decode (we log a kernel switch when sequence crosses 512/1024 thresholds). That caused some small jitter in p99.

samir: Where were the calibration stats taken from? Online calib vs offline can matter for FP8/INT4.

maya: I used online-minmax quick calib (per-batch) for INT8/FP8 and per-channel minmax for INT4 during a warmup set of 200 sequences. I also tried a conservative offline calib for FP8 and that improved quality but increased token latency by ~3% due to extra rescale ops.

olga: Do you have any failing prompt examples for the INT4 hallucinations? We should capture a diff-run with golden logits.

maya: Yep. Short example: knowledge-retrieval prompts where the model needs to copy exact entity strings at step ~1700. INT4 occasionally replaced numeric tokens with similar subwords. I'll drop one sanitized example below and a small log snippet.

```
PROMPT: "List invoice IDs between 2020-01 and 2020-03 for acct_XXXX"
FP16 OUTPUT: "... invoice 48321, 48900, 49512 ..."
INT4 OUTPUT:  "... invoice 48321, 49X00, 49512 ..."  <-- mis-decoded token
LOG: decode step 1723: topk diff at token 3 -> provable increase in perplexity
```

samir: Probable cause: quantized KV scales underflow for some keys at long caching horizons and the subsequent unquant/rescale noise pushes topk ordering. Did you try hybrid: INT4 for older prefixes, FP8 for recent KV entries?

maya: Yes — that was the next experiment. Hybrid policy: keep last 512 tokens in FP8, flush older KV to INT4. That regained decode quality in the sample prompts but increased memory ~6% vs full-INT4 and latency ~2%.

ryan: Interesting. Any impact on batching? We use continuous batching heuristics that assume stable kernel choice per batch. Frequent kernel switches might kill batching efficiency.

maya: Exactly. When the batch contains sequences that cross the kernel threshold (512/1024) we observed kernel-selection churn and kernel-launch overhead went up ~9% on p95. The profiler shows extra memcpy and kernel queue stalls when mixing quant formats in the same batch.

olga: Can we change the batching heuristic to group by "kv-quant bucket" first? Group sequences by effective kv-format (int4/fp8/int8/fp16) and seq-length bucket during batch assembly.

samir: We can. Proposal: when assembling a batch, compute a key: (target_kv_format, seq_bucket) and prefer fills that maximize same-key items, with a small age-based fairness cap so no one starves. Default seq_buckets: <=512, 513-1024, >1024.

maya: I prototyped that — results: mixed-batch kernel-switch stalls down 65%, effective throughput up 11% in our synthetic load, and fewer decode regressions caused by intra-batch format conversions.

ryan: Good. Two more asks: (1) add a flag to force per-request KV-format (so we can A/B test reliably) (2) log a compact per-request metric: kv-format, avg-kv-scale, percent-zero-scales, and kernel_churn_count.

maya: WIP — added `--kv-format-force` and `--log-kv-stats` to the bench. Sample log line:

```
req=3211 kvfmt=int4 avg_scale=0.023 pct_zero=0.004 churn=2 p50=7.4 p99=12.9 mem=9.1GB
```

olga: Can you drop the raw perf traces in the shared perf bucket? I'll run a longer A/B with user traffic replay tomorrow.

maya: Done. Uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/kv-quant/1755006789/ and left a note in the replay job with `--preserve-seed`.

perf-bot: Job replay-1755006789 completed: 1000 replays (traffic mode), AB test: INT4-hybrid vs INT4-full, delta decode-quality metric: INT4-hybrid +0.9% (fewer token mismatches), latency delta: hybrid +1.8% vs full-INT4.

samir: Ok next steps: 1) Ramp hybrid policy as opt-in in dedicated pools and run 24h traffic replays; 2) Implement batcher grouping by kv-format+seq_bucket; 3) Add kernel-selection hysteresis (don't switch kernel until sustained seq change > N tokens or >M ms) to reduce churn.

ryan: Add to eng-runtime board and assign follow-ups. Thanks maya, good work.

maya: Will open PRs for batcher and logs by end of day. Thanks all. :rocket:
